skill.name: research
skill.description: Investigate questions using primary sources, then save cited findings as a Markdown file that follows repository conventions.
skill.summary: Delegate primary-source research and capture cited findings in a repository Markdown file.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: Static analysis found no suspicious patterns, and semantic review found no prompt injection or harmful intent. The prompt-only skill contains no executable code.

content.value_statement: Technical research consumes time and often relies on unsupported secondary summaries. This skill delegates source review and saves cited findings in a repository Markdown file.
actual_capabilities: Delegates research to a background agent.
Prioritizes official documentation, source code, specifications, and first-party APIs.
Requires each claim to trace back to its owning source.
Writes findings and citations to one Markdown file.
Uses existing repository conventions when choosing the file location.
Reports the chosen location when no convention exists.
limitations: Requires an environment that supports background agents and repository file access.
Cannot guarantee that primary sources are available, complete, or current.
Does not define a required citation format or report structure.
Does not provide independent fact checking beyond tracing claims to sources.

use_cases.title: Verify API Behavior
use_cases.description: Trace an API question through official documentation, specifications, and source code, then save a cited technical note.

use_cases.title: Prepare Product Evidence
use_cases.description: Collect first-party evidence for a product decision and preserve the findings for later review.

use_cases.title: Build Documentation References
use_cases.description: Gather authoritative sources before drafting documentation, tutorials, or migration guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Research a Question
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate {question} using primary sources. Save a cited Markdown note that follows this repository's conventions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a focused question with a clear answer.

prompt_templates.title: Verify API Details
prompt_templates.prompt: Research how {API} handles {behavior}. Verify each claim with official documentation, specifications, first-party APIs, or source code, then save the findings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before implementing behavior that depends on API details.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Technical Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare {option A} and {option B} for {decision}. Use primary evidence, document gaps or disagreements, and save a decision-focused Markdown report.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a team needs evidence for a technical choice.

prompt_templates.title: Map Complex Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an evidence map for {complex question}. Trace conclusions through specifications, source code, documentation, and first-party APIs, recording uncertainty and conflicts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced research spanning several authoritative sources.

output_examples.input: Research whether an API guarantees stable result ordering.
output_examples.output: A Markdown note states the documented guarantee, cites the official reference, records source-code evidence, and identifies any unresolved ambiguity.

output_examples.input: Compare two migration approaches using primary evidence.
output: A concise comparison of supported behavior and constraints.
Citations to official documentation, specifications, or source code.
A section covering evidence gaps and uncertain conclusions.

output_examples.input: Find the authoritative explanation for a framework behavior.
output_examples.output: A repository note traces the behavior to its owning documentation or source code and provides citations for each claim.

best_practices: Ask a narrow question with explicit scope and decision criteria.
Prefer current first-party sources and record version or date context.
Review the saved note for citation accuracy before using its conclusions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat secondary articles as authoritative when primary sources exist.
Do not request broad research without defining the question or intended decision.
Do not present uncertain or conflicting evidence as a confirmed fact.

faq.question: What sources does this skill prioritize?
faq.answer: It prioritizes official documentation, source code, specifications, and first-party APIs.

faq.question: Where are the findings saved?
faq.answer: The skill follows existing repository conventions or chooses a sensible location and reports it.

faq.question: Does the skill include citations?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires every claim to trace back to the source that owns it.

faq.question: Can it research API behavior?
faq.answer: Yes, when official documentation, specifications, first-party APIs, or source code provide relevant evidence.

faq.question: Does it execute code or scripts?
faq.answer: No. The skill only instructs an agent to research sources and write a Markdown file.

faq.question: Can it resolve conflicting sources?
faq.answer: It can document conflicts, but users should review uncertain conclusions before making important decisions.
